chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abu Dawud, from some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I pass by a date-palm and eat from it.' He said, 'Eat, but do not carry (take away).' I said, 'May I be your ransom, the merchants have bought it and paid its price.' He said, 'They bought what is not theirs.'

key_terms.تَحْمِلْ: to carry/take away (indicating removal from the tree)
key_terms.مَا لَيْسَ لَهُمْ: what is not theirs (indicating lack of full ownership)
key_terms.نَقَدُوا: they paid (specifically cashed out or paid the full price)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating from a tree before the fruit is fully harvested or taken?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *Gharar* (uncertainty) in pre-harvest fruit sales, a key topic in Chapter 7 regarding *Bay' al-Thimar*. The Imam clarifies that while merchants may have paid the price, ownership remains incomplete until the fruit is fully ripe or harvested, preventing premature transfer of title. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on ensuring asset specificity and maturity in commercial contracts to avoid dispute.
